0. Input

Program:

final int STOP = -1;
int sum = 0, count = 0;
int x = StdIn.readInt();
while (x != STOP) {
    sum += x;
    count++;
    x = StdIn.readInt();
}
System.out.println(sum / count);

Question: Suppose the very first number typed is -1. What does the program print, and why?

Student's answer: 0. Nothing was added, so sum and count are both 0, and 0 divided by 0 is just 0. Settings: width 3, depth 3, prune llm, backend claude-cli, model claude-opus-5-5

The sentinel is never processed. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: A priming read comes before the loop, then each pass runs: test value != SENTINEL, process (sum += v; count++), then read the next value at the end of the body. An equivalent form is while (true) { v = read; if (v == SENTINEL) break; process; }. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L2#1 | level L2 way output_prediction: With input 3 -1 5 99999 7, keeping only non-negative values, the Rainfall average is (3+5)/2 = 4.0. The 7 after the sentinel is never read. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L2#2 | level L2 way one_step_execution: One pass reads one value. If it is the sentinel, the loop ends with sum and count unchanged; otherwise the (valid) value updates sum and count. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L3#0 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The sentinel test replaces, or is added to, the isEmpty() test. The average is computed once, after the loop. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L3#2 | level L3 way purpose_of_the_whole: Plan: Soloway's sentinel-controlled running-total loop (Rainfall). Roles: sum is a gatherer, count a stepper, and the value read a most-recent holder. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L4#0 | level L4 way predict_a_change: Changing the sentinel keeps the behaviour only if the new value cannot occur in the data. Moving the test after the processing step breaks the invariant that the sentinel is never processed. | | lvl:sentinel_loop@L4#1 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: Check count > 0 before computing sum / count. division_by_zero, level ways: 15 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | lvl:division_by_zero@L0#0 | level L0 way everyday_reading: Folk meaning: in maths division by zero is 'impossible', so every x / 0 must be rejected, ideally by the compiler. Java rule: the compiler accepts it; int or long / and % by zero throw ArithmeticException at run time, while double division by zero is legal and gives Infinity or NaN. | | lvl:division_by_zero@L0#3 | level L0 way inconsistent_trace: Points to LT (both operands are evaluated, promotion decides whether the division is int or double, and only then is the divisor checked). Applied unevenly: the student lets 1/0.0 crash because the 1 is an int, or lets 1/0 give Infinity on one line and an exception on another. (here mixing in: "Dividing by zero always stops the program with an error") | | lvl:division_by_zero@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: Division by zero is the evaluation of x / 0 or x % 0: a run-time error for integer types and a special value (Infinity or NaN) for floating-point types. | | lvl:division_by_zero@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: An integer / or % throws ArithmeticException if the right operand is zero; floating-point arithmetic follows IEEE 754, so a nonzero double divided by zero is Infinity or -Infinity and 0.0/0.0 is NaN. With doubles, 1.0 / 0.0 is Infinity and 0.0 / 0.0 (or Math.sqrt(-1.0)) is NaN; NaN is not equal to anything, not even itself. | | lvl:division_by_zero@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: Left operand, then right operand are fully evaluated; then the division itself runs: for int it checks the divisor and throws at that moment, so the rest of the statement (the assignment or the println) never happens; for double it produces the special value and evaluation continues. | | lvl:division_by_zero@L2#1 | level L2 way output_prediction: 1/0 and 1%0 produce no value: the program stops with Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero; 1.0/0.0 is Infinity, -1.0/0.0 is -Infinity, 0.0/0.0 is NaN, and 1/0.0 is Infinity (the 1 is promoted). | | lvl:division_by_zero@L2#2 | level L2 way one_step_execution: For int, no variable changes: the exception aborts the statement and (uncaught) ends the program.
